variants.headline: Both sides in sight near {{city}}
body: Our observers counted {{ourUnits}} of our regiments and {{theirUnits}} from {{opponent}} in the {{domain}} zone near {{city}}. If both sides stay in the area, either could contest the approaches. Whoever holds the ground and brings up support first will decide them.

variants.headline: The {{domain}} zone at {{city}}, entered
body: The observer's book lists {{ourUnits}} of our regiments and {{theirUnits}} from {{opponent}} in the {{domain}} zone at {{city}}. Our assessment was {{posture}}, and it weighs positions and support as much as the count. Who holds the approaches remains a question for the next entry.

variants.headline: What the count near {{city}} leaves out
body: The latest sighting places {{ourUnits}} of our regiments and {{theirUnits}} from {{opponent}} in the {{domain}} zone near {{city}}. Anyone reading the tally should ask who has the ground and who can bring up support. Neither answer is in the ledger, and until one is, the approaches belong to whoever moves first.

variants.headline: Barbarians in sight of {{city}}
body: Smoke from the raiders' fires has been rising beyond the ridge above {{city}}, and the watch counts {{barbarians}} of them. The last farm outside the wall was abandoned at midday, its door still open. The garrison has shut the north gate and sent for help.

variants.headline: Hear it, {{city}}! Raiders at the walls
body: Raiders on the ridge! {{barbarians}} of them, and the watch has seen their fires! Drive the herds inside and bar every shutter! Let no child stray past the gate! We hold the wall! We hold the wall!

variants.headline: Barbarians at {{city}} gates
body: Women in {{city}} packed bread and water into sacks. They left them at the gate for the defenders. An old man said he had seen barbarians before. He told the young to keep their voices low.

variants.headline: Counting raiders at {{city}}
body: The watch has fixed a figure on the raiders around {{city}}: {{barbarians}}. A band of that size must scatter to feed itself, which means the farms outside the wall will suffer before the town does. Driving them off is a bill the harvest can barely cover, and the town will pay it in grain either way.

variants.headline: At {{city}}, the garrison answers: {{posture}}
body: {{city}}'s town book lists raiders in the fields, {{barbarians}} by the watch's count. The captain's answer is written in the margin: {{posture}}. That evening the outer farms were emptied and the gate was barred before the stars appeared.

variants.headline: {{city}} goes hungry under siege
body: Food in {{city}} is running short, and the siege has begun to show at every table. A porter at the grain exchange says the sacks now weigh less than their labels promise. The city is counting meals by the week, and the count is falling.

variants.headline: Who can still buy supper in {{city}}?
body: Hunger in {{city}} falls harder on some tables than others. The families who buy flour daily will feel the siege first, while a merchant with a full cellar can wait a month. The stalls still stand, but coin gives out before grain, and when the last purse is empty the stalls will go with it.

variants.headline: In {{city}}, the queue starts before dawn
body: {{terms.civic.people}} of {{city}}, the baker has begun cutting loaves smaller and saying nothing about it. The queue forms before dawn, and every customer watches the scale. Ask him how long the flour will last, and he answers by tapping the empty barrel behind the counter.

variants.headline: To the faithful of {{city}}: hold fast
body: To the faithful in {{city}}: the granaries are nearly bare and the gates must remain shut. Throw open the shrines to anyone without a warm room, and share what bread you can spare. The season will turn, and what is given now will not be forgotten.

variants.headline: The walls of {{city}} are failing
body: Half of the wall of {{city}}, held by {{civilization}}, is down, and its rubble lies in the streets. A carter who passed beneath the gate said he could see the sky through the breach. The defenders have not begun repairs, which suggests they have given up on the outer wall.

variants.headline: An accounting of {{city}}
body: City examined: {{city}}, held by {{civilization}}.
Wall standing: half of it at best.
Verdict: the next storm will finish what the siege began.

variants.headline: Abroad tonight: heavy damage at {{city}}
body: Word from abroad tonight: half of {{city}}'s wall, held by {{civilization}}, is down. Engineers say the breach is wide enough to march through. The city still flies its flag, but the stone no longer argues for it.

variants.headline: The walls of a rival come down
body: {{city}} belongs to {{civilization}}, and half of its wall is down. Stone in that condition turns a battle into a question of nerve, because the defenders must now choose where to make their fight. If {{civilization}} has a reserve, this is the week to show it.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} prepares offensive actions
body: Observers report that {{civilization}} has transitioned from {{previousPosture}} to a {{posture}} posture on {{observedTurn}}, most notable in {{city}}'s {{domain}} area. The move indicates a shift in the priorities of {{civilization}}'s high command.

variants.headline: From {{previousPosture}} to {{posture}} at {{city}}
body: The front assessment for {{city}}, held by {{civilization}}, moved from {{previousPosture}} to {{posture}} on {{observedTurn}}. The reading covers the {{domain}} zone, and it turned offensive before any formation was seen to move. If the balance our observers measured holds, the next days should show the assault itself.

variants.headline: {{observedTurn}}: the entry for {{city}}
body: In the campaign record, {{observedTurn}} marks a change from {{previousPosture}} to {{posture}} in our assessment of the {{domain}} zone at {{city}}, held by {{civilization}}. The cause is unrecorded.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} IS COMING!
body: {{civilization}} has stopped playing games. Reports from {{observedTurn}} show they have adopted a {{posture}} in the {{domain}}. The people of {{city}} remember when the enemy was just {{previousPosture}}. Now, the only thing coming our way is steel.

variants.headline: The posture reading from {{city}}
body: The front assessment for {{city}}, held by {{civilization}}, moved to {{posture}} in the {{domain}} area on {{observedTurn}}. That is a dated reading of posture, not an order being carried out in the city. Our agent is there now, and the war office has entered the change. A posture is a warning in itself; whether it becomes a march is not yet known.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} regrouping near {{city}}
body: After a period of {{previousPosture}}, {{civilization}} has adopted a {{posture}} posture near {{city}}'s {{domain}} area {{observedTurn}}. Military analysts believe the enemy is now attempting to stabilize its front.

variants.headline: The Enemy Recovers
body: After a period of {{previousPosture}}, {{civilization}} has adopted a {{posture}} posture in the {{domain}} area of {{city}} as of {{observedTurn}}. The retreat is over, and the enemy is now stabilizing its lines. This regrouping is a warning: we must not mistake their reorganization for weakness.

variants.headline: The board at {{city}} is updated
body: The front board for {{city}} was updated on {{observedTurn}}. The reading moved from {{previousPosture}} to {{posture}} in the {{domain}} area, and the city is held by {{civilization}}. In plain words: the force our watchers saw pulling back has stopped and is being put in order again.

variants.headline: A False Retreat at {{city}}!
body: On {{observedTurn}}, the {{civilization}} ceased their {{previousPosture}} to {{posture}} in the {{domain}} area. Was the withdrawal just a trick to lure us into a false sense of security? Our {{terms.civic.people}} cannot sleep while the enemy gathers strength so close to {{city}}. Stop the talk in the council and send the guards now!

variants.headline: {{civilization}} Withdraws from {{domain}}
body: As of {{observedTurn}}, military reports indicate that {{civilization}} has shifted its posture to {{posture}} near {{city}}'s {{domain}} area. Their forces had previously maintained a {{previousPosture}} posture. While this movement leaves the region around {{city}} quieter, it remains unclear if the shift is permanent or tactical.

variants.headline: A Strategic Retreat, or a Trap?
body: The forces of {{civilization}} abandoned their {{previousPosture}} posture in the {{domain}} on {{observedTurn}}, withdrawing from the vicinity of {{city}}. While the {{terms.civic.government}} hails this as a victory, we must ask if it is a trap or a sign of a deeper collapse in the enemy's line. Moving too quickly into the vacuum could leave our own forces exposed to a counter-strike.

variants.headline: Movement on the Front
body: The forces of {{civilization}} have withdrawn from their position in the {{domain}} near {{city}}. This change from a {{previousPosture}} posture was observed on {{observedTurn}}.

variants.headline: QUIET AT LAST?
body: A lookout in {{city}} saw {{civilization}} army started to leave the {{domain}} on {{observedTurn}}. They spent weeks in a {{previousPosture}} posture, eyeing our walls. Now the dust settles, and the tavern is full of people asking where the war went.

variants.headline: Enemy Troops Sighted Near {{city}}
body: Regiments from {{enemies}} have been spotted in the vicinity of {{city}}. Local scouts confirmed the presence of these forces today, and garrison forces are reportedly on alert. The {{terms.civic.government}} has been notified of the sighting.

variants.headline: ENEMIES APPROACHING
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}! The {{enemies}} are at our doorstep in {{city}}! Gather your courage and your weapons. Fight for {{terms.civilization}}, fight for your homes!

variants.headline: Emergency at {{city}}
body: {{city}} is now under direct threat as {{enemies}} move their forces into the immediate vicinity. By placing pressure on {{city}}, the enemy is testing our reaction time and our resolve. Firmness now is the only way to deter a full-scale assault on our {{owner.civic.people}}.

variants.headline: Sightings near {{city}}
body: Troops from {{enemies}} are now near {{city}}. Local defenses are responding and the government has been notified. Check the latest reports for troop strength.

variants.headline: {{count|enemy unit|enemy units}} destroyed in the field
body: The latest fighting cost {{victim}} {{count|regiment|regiments}}, every one of them marching under the same standard. Our soldiers have stacked the captured colors beside the gate, and the pile reaches a man's shoulder. {{victim}} will need a season to replace what fell in an afternoon.

variants.headline: The enemy's losses, counted
body: {{victim}} regiments destroyed: {{count}}.
Standards taken: one design, repeated.
Balance of the season: entered in our favor.

variants.headline: {{count|enemy unit|enemy units}} destroyed in the fighting
body: From the front tonight: our troops have destroyed {{count|regiment|regiments}} of {{victim}}. Every one of them marched under the same flag, and that flag now hangs in our camp. A season of recruiting will not replace what an afternoon took.

variants.headline: Hear it! {{count|enemy unit|enemy units}} destroyed
body: Gather and hear the count! {{count}} regiments of {{victim}} are broken on the field! Their banners fill a cart, and their families will learn the number soon enough! Tell it in the square and sing it in every tavern!

variants.headline: {{city}} falls to {{winner}}
body: News has come that {{winner}} has taken {{city}}, the capital of {{loser}}, by force. The report arrived with a ship's cargo, and the customs clerk read it twice before entering the duty. The fighting is elsewhere, but the prices it moves are not.

variants.headline: After {{city}} falls, who holds authority?
body: {{city}}, the seat of {{loser}}, now answers to {{winner}}. A government can lose its capital and keep its authority, or keep the buildings and lose the habit of command. Watch which officials still report to which office, and the answer will show itself.

variants.headline: The fall of a capital
body: The year's record states that {{winner}} took by arms {{city}}, the capital of {{loser}}. The keeper of the rolls entered the fall beside the accounts of plague and drought. Prayer was ordered for the city's people, and no cause was written.

variants.headline: Abroad tonight: {{city}} falls
body: Abroad tonight, {{winner}} has seized {{city}}, the capital of {{loser}}. New maps will be needed by morning, and every court that watches the map will be busy before the week ends.

variants.headline: A capital falls near our own border
body: A capital has fallen near our border: {{winner}} has taken {{capitalDescription}}. Refugees have already been seen on the road, carrying what they could tie to a cart. Our frontier posts are counting them as they pass.

variants.headline: What {{winner}}'s capture means here
body: When {{winner}} took {{capitalDescription}}, it gained more than buildings. It gained the offices, the archives and the habit of obedience that gather in a capital. The question now is whether the displaced government can rule from another city.

variants.headline: The fall of a capital near our borders
body: The annals record that {{winner}} captured {{capitalDescription}} in this year. The court scribe wrote the entry in a steady hand and left a space beside it for the terms. That space remains empty, and the border has been quiet since.

variants.headline: A capital just fell near us
body: Capital down: {{winner}} has taken {{capitalDescription}}. It is close to us. Watch the roads.

variants.headline: {{winner}} Secures Control of {{city}}
body: {{winner}} has seized {{city}} from {{loser}}. News of the conquest reached {{terms.civilizationAdjective}} capital this morning. The city has now transitioned to the administration of {{winner}}.

variants.headline: The Fall of {{city}}
body: The capture of {{city}} by {{winner}} has redrawn the regional map, bringing the front line just {{distance}} from our own borders. This victory gives {{winner}} a dominant tactical position over {{loser}}, threatening trade routes and settlements. Whether this serves as a buffer or a bridgehead for further aggression, {{terms.civilization}} must now reckon with the reality of {{winner}}'s expanded ambition.

variants.headline: Conquest in {{city}}
body: We are informed that {{city}}, located {{distance}} from our borders, has been seized by {{winner}} from the control of {{loser}}.

variants.headline: {{winner}} AT OUR DOORSTEP!
body: {{winner}} has seized {{city}} from {{loser}}. Refugees are already streaming in, as the enemy is only {{distance}} from here. We can hear the drums; our walls better be strong.

variants.headline: {{neighbor}}'s army now outranks ours
body: The army of {{neighbor}} now outnumbers ours, according to the count kept at the war office. The clerks ran the figures twice before sending them up. No one there would say the gap is small.

variants.headline: The tally of arms
body: Our strength: {{ourStrength}}.
Their strength: {{theirStrength}}.
The balance: theirs, for the first time this season.

variants.headline: Ask why {{neighbor}}'s army passed ours
body: {{neighbor}} has passed us in the count of arms, and the {{terms.civic.government}} has not explained how. The {{terms.civic.people}} pay for every regiment we raise, and they are entitled to know what our money bought. Either the count is wrong or the policy is.

variants.headline: The balance of arms has turned
body: In this season the army of {{neighbor}} exceeded our own in number. The war office entered the change without comment, as it enters the weather. The frontier regiments were ordered to stand their ground and report.

variants.headline: The strength rating from {{neighbor}}
body: Military strength is an assessed figure, not a count of soldiers, and the assessment now puts {{neighbor}} above us. Our agent is in that country, where the drill yards and the roads give a reader something to weigh. The war office holds a rating it can defend, and the rating is not in our favor.

variants.headline: Our army passes {{neighbor}}'s
body: The war office count now puts our army above {{neighbor}}'s. The new figure was posted on the board, and an officer stood looking at it longer than the others. He said only that the lead would have to be used before it was spent.

variants.headline: Our arms in good order
body: Letters from the war office state that our forces now exceed those of {{neighbor}} in the field. The return was read at the war office and entered without ceremony. A lead in numbers is a tool; what matters is the hand that holds it.

variants.headline: Our army just passed {{neighbor}}'s
body: Count changed: our army is bigger than {{neighbor}}'s now. The board at the war office says so. Somebody should tell the enemy.

variants.headline: The account of strength
body: Our strength: {{ourStrength}}.
Their strength: {{theirStrength}}.
The balance: ours, by the difference.

variants.headline: {{city}} Suffers Heavy Damage
body: {{city}} has sustained significant damage during recent hostilities. Labor teams have begun assessing the wreckage to determine the extent of the losses, while priority is being given to the city's fortifications.

variants.headline: The Crumbled Promise of {{city}}
body: The walls of {{city}} have fallen to a shocking degree of ruin. The {{owner.civic.government}} spoke of an impenetrable shield, yet the current strength of the fortifications is a fraction of what was promised. This failure of intelligence and defense leaves the {{owner.civic.people}} exposed. {{owner.civic.leaderAddress}}, where was the protection we were guaranteed?

variants.headline: Half of {{city}} is patching cracks tonight
body: {{city}} took heavy damage and the street lamps flicker low. An old man nailed boards over his shop window and told his boy to sleep downstairs. The square is quiet, and nobody sings.

variants.headline: HOLD THE LINE
body: Attention, {{terms.civic.people}}! The streets of {{city}} lie in ruins! Do not falter, for the survival of {{terms.civilization}} depends on our resolve. Hold the line!

variants.headline: {{city}} prepares to push back
body: The defense of {{city}} has evolved. As of {{observedTurn}}, the {{terms.civic.government}} has ordered a move from {{previousPosture}} to a {{posture}} posture.

variants.headline: The Tide Turns at {{city}}
body: On {{observedTurn}}, our forces near {{city}} transitioned from a {{previousPosture}} stance to {{posture}} in the {{domain}}. The period of absorbing the enemy's blows is over, as we are seizing the initiative and forcing the enemy onto their heels. We have weathered the storm; now we are the storm.

variants.headline: A change on the board at {{city}}
body: The front board for {{city}} shows a new entry tonight, dated {{observedTurn}}. The reading moved from {{previousPosture}} to {{posture}} in the {{domain}} zone. The force that dug in around the city now means to come out and strike.

variants.headline: Our line at {{city}} is read anew
body: Dispatches from the map room state that the front at {{city}} has been reassessed from {{previousPosture}} to {{posture}}, with the change entered on {{observedTurn}}. The dispatch describes the {{domain}} zone and offers no forecast. We print the entry as it stands.

variants.headline: Defensive measures increased in {{city}}
body: Military reports indicate that {{city}} transitioned to a {{posture}} posture on {{observedTurn}}. The shift from {{previousPosture}} reflects a renewed emphasis on city fortifications.

variants.headline: The Gates of {{city}} Barred
body: Letters from the district relate that {{city}} has shifted to {{posture}}, leaving behind its {{previousPosture}} disposition. While the {{terms.civic.government}} claims this ensureth the safety of the realm, the {{terms.civic.people}} must wonder why such a desperate measure became necessary.

variants.headline: Defense of {{city}}
body: Hear me, {{terms.civic.people}}! The army is no longer marching forward. They are digging in right here in {{city}} to hold the line. We are the shield now! The shield of {{terms.civilization}}!

variants.headline: The Defensive Disposition of {{city}}
body: At {{observedTurn}}, the {{terms.civic.government}} ordered the forces in {{city}} to adopt a {{posture}} posture. This shift from {{previousPosture}} was executed within {{city}}'s {{domain}} area, as recorded by the {{terms.civic.government}}'s scribes.

variants.headline: {{count}} of our regiments lost in action
body: The latest fighting with {{killer}} cost us {{count|regiment|regiments}}. The news reached the war office in a single dispatch, and the clerk who copied it left the room without speaking. The lists of names will take longer to prepare than the count did.

variants.headline: Our losses, counted
body: Regiments lost to {{killer}}: {{count}}.
Names entered: still being copied.
The account: not yet closed.

variants.headline: The empty bunks
body: At the barracks, the sergeant walked down the row of bunks and did not stop at {{count|regiment|regiments}} of them, every one lost to {{killer}}. The blankets are folded and the kits are gone, and he has not yet asked for replacements. He says the room is quieter than it used to be.

variants.headline: The count from the fighting
body: They say {{killer}} took {{count}} of our regiments. I heard it from a man who was there, and he would not say more than the number. The families will hear the rest soon enough.
